2608.25717.title: When RAG Fails to Equalize: Geo-bias in Factual Question Answering over Public Companies
2608.25717.paper_summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is widely assumed to mitigate factual errors in large language models (LLMs), but it remains unclear whether retrieval uniformly compensates for missing knowledge. We study this question in a controlled factual QA setting over public companies, constructing a benchmark of approximately 2,000 firms across global equity indices. We evaluate six LLMs on four atomic attributes under four conditions: no-context, perfect context, misleading context, and distraction context. We find strong geographic disparities in no-context accuracy, indicating uneven parametric knowledge. While perfect context improves performance, it does not eliminate these gaps: gains are correlated with baseline accuracy, suggesting retrieval effectiveness is coupled to internal representations. Under misleading context, models frequently copy incorrect information. Larger models improve overall performance but do not remove these structural effects. These results challenge the view of RAG as a universal corrective and highlight the interaction between model knowledge, context quality, and entity representation.
2608.25717.paper_summary_zh: 檢索增強生成（RAG）普遍被認為能減少大型語言模型（LLMs）中的事實錯誤，但尚不清楚檢索是否均勻地彌補了缺失的知識。<lb/>我們在一個受控的事實問答環境中研究這個問題，針對公共公司構建了一個約2,000家公司的基準，涵蓋全球股權指數。<lb/>我們在四種條件下評估六個LLM的四個原子屬性：無上下文、完美上下文、誤導性上下文和干擾上下文。<lb/>我們發現在無上下文的準確性上存在強烈的地理差異，表明參數知識的不均勻性。<lb/>雖然完美上下文提高了性能，但並未消除這些差距：增益與基線準確性相關，這表明檢索的有效性與內部表徵相互關聯。<lb/>在誤導性上下文下，模型經常複製不正確的信息。<lb/>較大的模型提高了整體性能，但並未消除這些結構性影響。<lb/>這些結果挑戰了將RAG視為普遍修正的觀點，並突顯了模型知識、上下文質量和實體表徵之間的相互作用。
